title: Write the AddBiomechanics acquisition and one-row-per-frame converter for Falisse and both Tan studies

decision_context.D-HIST-04-1: A: one row per frame from the dynamics pass
decision_context.D-HIST-04-2: A: no contact; drop Falisse subject_1, subject_7, subject_8

summary: Fixture-only build; no download, no launch. New acquisition script streams one archive member by HTTP range (pinned ETag, exact 206), checks the local header against the central directory, inflates straight to one B3D (no compressed copy), checks CRC32, SHA-256 (streamed and re-read) and, where HIST-04 read it, the Drive header SHA-256, then the layout arithmetic. It then converts and deletes the B3D. Only one B3D may exist under the transient root (peak 2.22 GB, Tan running s3); a failed attempt keeps it as .rejected, which blocks the next job. New converter writes one row per frame from the pass whose recorded type is 'dynamics' in each trial's pass header (never by index); a trial without exactly one dynamics pass writes no rows and is counted. All frames are kept with their missing-GRF reason. Metadata follow the HIST-04 table. Timesteps are not rounded. Absent fields stay absent. Entered and dynamics-model masses are columns; normalization_mass_kg stays missing pending José's convention. Signals keep source names: DOF-index columns, contact-body names, world frame. reference_side is 'none' with no ipsi/contra columns; canonical mapping is a later step. Falisse subject_1, 7 and 8 are refused by both scripts. 33 plan-only specs regenerated with the real script hashes; validate_spec passed for each.
local_artifacts: converted_datasets/reconversion_v2/hist05_addbiomechanics_20261101/plans_r3/ (current: 33 specs + 01b release spec, expected files, index.json)

design.frame_decoder: Own protobuf wire decoder, not nimblephysics. It follows the record layout in nimblephysics SubjectOnDisk.cpp at c405b056 (write 415-500, readFrames 960-1065): each frame is a sensor record, then one pass record per trial pass in that trial's pass order. The dynamics record offset is sensor + k x pass size, where k is the index of 'dynamics' in that trial's pass headers.
design.columns: Identity, task, task_info and subject_metadata JSON; trial, split and frame indices; time_s = frame x source timestep; source_timestep_s; dynamics marker RMS and linear/angular residuals (per-frame header arrays); missing_grf_reason. Signals: dofNN_pos/vel/acc/tau; <body>_force/cop/torque_xyz for each contact body (world frame); com_pos/vel/acc_xyz; root_residual_0-5.
design.not_written: Raw sensor record and the kinematics and low-pass passes (per D-HIST-04-1). From the dynamics pass: ground_contact_wrench, joint centres and the root-frame copies other than the residual. Listed in each conversion.json.
design.task: Falisse task null (unresolved). Tan running task 'run' with tokens only. Tan walking task null (level_walking versus dynamic_walk pending), with a modification token. speed_m_s and incline_deg are listed as unavailable, never filled.
design.address_space: 768 MiB in the specs: pyarrow fails to allocate under 256 MiB RLIMIT_AS (checked).

checks: 17 synthetic tests (tests/test_hist05_addbiomechanics_member.py). The fake B3D is built with the test's own protobuf encoder: 3 trials with different pass orders, one without a dynamics pass. Values encode pass, trial and frame; the B3D is served from an in-memory fake archive behind a deflated local header.

End to end: the dynamics values are chosen in both pass orders (pass index 2 and 0); the trial without a dynamics pass is counted as excluded (2 frames); the B3D is deleted; the outputs are exactly frames.parquet, conversion.json and dynamics_model.osim.

Metadata: time_s equals frame x the unrounded timestep 0.009947643979057591; mass, height, sex and age come from the header; the model masses are 60/80 kg; normalization_mass_kg is missing; missing_grf_reason names are mapped; the split index is in task_info.
Absent fields: age and data_quality are absent when not in the file; treadmill and speed are not filled for Falisse.

Refusals: dropped subjects 1, 7 and 8 are refused before any network call; a central-directory CRC mismatch, a payload CRC mismatch while streaming (kept as .rejected), a Drive header-hash mismatch, a changed ETag, an existing output root, existing converter outputs, short disk (refused before download), another B3D already under the transient root, and a layout mismatch.

Real headers (no frames): the converter's parse_header and layout reproduce the file size for 15 of 15 HIST-04 headers. Every trial has exactly one dynamics pass, and the per-frame missing-GRF and dynamics-pass arrays have trial length.

rework.R1_pass_order: convert() now excludes, with a logged reason and frame count, any trial whose pass list differs from the file-wide pass list at the same positions. nimblephysics labels records by the file-wide list, so the two readers cannot disagree. Tests: the mismatched-order fixture trial (Mis_1) is excluded, and with a file-wide order of kinematics, dynamics, lowPassFilter the dynamics record is still found by name (index 1).
rework.R2_pilot_retained: Spec 01 (Falisse subject_4) adds --keep-source-for-comparison: the B3D is kept (status converted_source_retained_for_comparison) and listed in expected_output_names. Every later run refuses while any receipt with that status lacks comparison_release.json. That holds even if the B3D was deleted by hand; the one-B3D-on-disk rule also blocks. New 'release-pilot RECEIPT_DIR COMPARISON.json' requires b3d_sha256 equal to the pilot's, a named reader and compared_frames > 0. It deletes the B3D (after re-hashing it) only for status 'agree'; otherwise it writes comparison_record.json, keeps the file and keeps blocking. Tests cover blocking, disagree-keeps-blocking, deletion without a record still blocks, release unblocks, and a comparison for another B3D refused.
rework.hardening: Dropped subjects are matched by (study, subject) ignoring split, case, spacing, leading zeros, repeated slashes and './' (is_dropped; tests for 4 aliases and 2 kept members). Each run re-checks its expected entry against the hash-checked central directory before any receipt or network call (test).

rework_round_2.G1_computed_comparison: release-pilot RECEIPT_DIR NEW_OUT_DIR takes no comparison file. It first re-hashes the retained B3D and frames.parquet against the pilot receipt. It then reads every written trial with nimblephysics SubjectOnDisk.readFrames (reader only; no writer setters) and picks the record nimblephysics labels DYNAMICS, which must sit at the parquet's pass index. Every signal column (dofNN pos/vel/acc/tau, per-body force/CoP/torque, COM pos/vel/acc, root residual) is compared with exact equality; NaN only matches NaN. It checks full coverage: the trial set equals the written trials, rows per trial equal the conversion record, and frames compared equal the receipt rows (738 expected for the pilot). It writes comparison.json (counts, mismatch examples, nimblephysics version, B3D/parquet/conversion/script/converter hashes) to the new folder. It deletes the B3D only if there are 0 mismatches and coverage is full, then writes comparison_release.json. On disagreement it writes comparison_record.json, keeps the B3D and stays blocked. A release record only unblocks if it holds such a complete agreeing comparison for this pilot's hashes and row count, and the B3D is gone; a hand-written record does not.
rework_round_2.G2_fixed_roots: CLI --run refuses unless --transient-root is DEST, the receipt dir sits directly under DEST/acquisition_receipts and --out is inside DEST. run() always checks DEST (fixed_root) for pending pilots and leftover B3Ds, in addition to the passed roots.

Sanity read of the released forces (one STS_2 trial, 7.36 s at about 100.1 Hz): the summed vertical force of calcn_r, calcn_l and pelvis averages 623.7 N over all frames and 635.2 N over the 269 frames flagged notMissingGRF, against 629.8 N body weight from the entered 64.2 kg (-1.0% and +0.9%) and 585.0 N from the dynamics-model mass of 59.6 kg. 467 of 738 frames (63%) are flagged footContactDetectedButNoForce and 2 missingBlip; they are kept and labelled. Not compared: the raw per-plate readings (not in the release; B3D now deleted).

falisse_run.procedure: Each job in its own tool call: plain dry run (output kept, status checked by grep), one launch, verify-cleanup, then a read-only summary run with python3 -I from /tmp after the launcher exited. Before this run, one dry run of 02 was refused because I had piped the launcher output into python3 -c with the repository as cwd (the census counts that as a worker). It was reported; the coordinator approved the procedure above. No later refusal.

falisse_run.tan_running_time_budget: Measured: the downloads ran at about the 2 MiB/s ceiling (2.10 MB/s). Wall minus transfer at the ceiling leaves about 4-5 s per 4,000-5,200 frames, roughly 1 ms per frame, which includes converting, the two SHA-256 re-reads and the parquet hash. Tan running s3 (largest): 1,640,560,231 B is 782 s at the ceiling, plus about 273 s for 273,092 frames, plus about 30-60 s for re-reading 2.2 GB twice: about 1,100-1,150 s, roughly a third of the 3,400 s script deadline (launcher timeout 3,600 s). The deadline is reached only if the server delivers less than about 0.53 MB/s. The Falisse files are small, so the per-frame and re-read costs at Tan scale are extrapolated; Tan walking (09-25, about 580 MB and 93,000 frames each, about 280 + 95 s) will measure them before any Tan running job.

tan_running_run.likely_cause_not_verified: The converter's header parse keeps per-frame arrays for all three passes (marker RMS, linear and angular residuals) and the missing-GRF list as Python lists. For s8 that is 241,173 frames x (3 passes x 3 arrays + 1), about 2.4 million Python floats and ints, plus the 18 MB header bytes and the pass model texts. Tan walking has 93,000 frames. Keeping only the dynamics-pass arrays, as compact arrays, would cut this. Not measured.

follow_ups.title: Reduce converter header-array memory (future converter revision)
follow_ups.note: parse_header keeps per-frame marker_rms, linear_residual and angular_residual for every pass, plus missing_grf, as Python lists (about 2.4 million objects for Tan running s8, peak RSS 407.5 MiB). Keep only the dynamics-pass arrays and store them as array('f')/array('B') or numpy. Needs a reviewed converter change, new spec hashes and a re-pilot; do not mix code hashes within a study's run.

Known case: Tan running s7 hip_calibration (1 segment, 2,000 frames), currently written as task 'run'. Release of calibration trials is undecided.
